title: Resisted Cross-Body Sit-Up Test
purpose: Provocation test for core muscle injury (CMI, athletic pubalgia, 'sports hernia'), the pubic-related entity of the Doha agreement on groin pain in athletes.
structure: Rectus abdominis and adductor longus insertions on the pubis; abdominal wall weakening without a true hernia.
procedure: Patient supine. The examiner stands on the affected side and places the affected leg in a figure-four position, then puts one hand on the patient's contralateral shoulder and the other on the affected-side knee. The patient brings the contralateral shoulder toward the affected-side knee (cross-body sit-up) against the examiner's resistance.

accuracy.source: Kurowicki et al. 2020, Am J Sports Med (diagnostic cohort, 3 tests for CMI)

notes: Very low specificity, so the source rates it as moderate value with many false positives and recommends using it in a cluster, together with a consistent history and positive diagnostic ultrasound. Differential: femoroacetabular impingement, lumbar or SIJ referred pain. Companion tests: straight leg sit-up test, external rotation Stinchfield test.

title: Straight Leg Sit-Up Test
purpose: Provocation test for core muscle injury (athletic pubalgia, 'sports hernia') or inguinal hernia within the pubic-related groin pain entity of the Doha agreement.
structure: Rectus abdominis and adductor longus insertions on the pubis; abdominal wall.
procedure: Patient supine. The patient lifts both extended legs and the shoulders 20-25 cm (8-10 inches) off the table at the same time.

accuracy.source: Kurowicki et al. 2020, Am J Sports Med (diagnostic cohort, 3 tests for CMI)

notes: Poor likelihood ratios: the source rates the stand-alone value as weak and advises a cluster with history and diagnostic ultrasound. Differential: femoroacetabular impingement, lumbar or SIJ referred pain. Companion tests: resisted cross-body sit-up test, external rotation Stinchfield test.
